items.explanation: Comprehensive means covering all aspects and all places, which both clauses require: every village, and health, schooling and roads together. Extensive means large in scale, which could describe one thing spread wide. Widespread means spread over an area, which says nothing about the range of needs, and thorough means carefully done, which says nothing about coverage.
items.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the word in the sentence. The relief reached every village, not just the towns on the main road, because the plan was ___: it covered health, schooling and roads rather than a single need.

items.explanation: Scrutinised means examined very carefully in detail, which both clauses show: checking against delivery notes, not just totals, and finding errors three reviewers missed. Examined and reviewed are general words for looking over something, and inspected suggests a formal check of condition rather than a line-by-line examination.
items.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the word in the sentence. The auditor ___ every invoice before signing off, checking each one against the delivery notes and not just the totals, and found two errors that three earlier reviewers had missed.

items.explanation: Dogged means stubbornly persistent, refusing to give up on a point. Only the third sentence shows that: the negotiator keeps returning to the same point through six rounds until it is answered. Giving up after the first round, changing demands every hour, and accepting the first offer to end the talks quickly are all ways of giving up, not of persisting.
options: The dogged negotiator gave up after the first round when the other side refused.
The dogged negotiator changed her demands every hour to suit the other side.
The dogged negotiator kept returning to the same point through six rounds until the other side answered it.
The dogged negotiator accepted the first offer to end the talks quickly.
items.question: Which sentence uses the word DOGGED correctly?

items.explanation: To cut corners means to save time or money by skipping proper steps, at a cost to quality. Only the last sentence has both parts: proper steps were skipped in the audit, and the cost appeared when errors were found. The first sentence is a literal shortcut, not a skipped proper step. The second sentence contradicts the idiom, since full quality checks mean no steps were skipped. The third sentence is merely saving money; booking a cheap hotel skips no proper step of the holiday.
options: He cut corners by taking the shorter road home from work.
They cut corners and delivered the project early with full quality checks.
She cut corners on her holiday by booking the cheapest hotel.
She cut corners on the audit and the errors were discovered within a week.
items.question: Choose the sentence in which the idiom 'to cut corners' is used correctly.
items.stream_verdict: OLD: match an idiom to a paraphrase of its meaning. NEW: correct-use judgement requiring both parts of the idiom (skipped step, quality cost). COLD-SOLVE: D, matches key. CHECKLIST: each distractor fails a different part of the idiom's meaning.

items.explanation: Step 1, blank (i): the archive holds letters from every year of the war, and letters are the record of daily life, so an account built on it alone would be detailed about daily life, not silent. Step 2, blank (ii): almost none of the letters come from the generals who directed the war, so the same account would have almost nothing to say about command decisions, and would be silent about them, not authoritative, since authority about command would need the generals' own record. Step 3, blank (iii): the two clauses together fix the archive's description, since letters from every year make it extensive, while the missing generals' letters mean it is not complete, so extensive is right and complete is wrong. Only the second option survives all three blanks: the first fails blank (iii), the third swaps blanks (i) and (ii), and the fourth fails blanks (ii) and (iii).
items.question: Choose the set of words that best completes the sentence. The archive held letters from every year of the war, yet almost none from the generals who directed it. A historian who relied on it alone would therefore write an account that was (i)______ about daily life and (ii)______ about command decisions, and the archive itself could best be described as (iii)______.
items.stream_verdict: REBUILD (pre-judged FAIL in sample 8, ChatGPT and judges agreed): old archetype Critical Reasoning assumption, single necessary-assumption move; new archetype Text Completion with three blanks, each resolved from a different clause, with blank (iii) depending on both clauses. Cold-solved from stem; key verified by reasoning check.

items.explanation: 'Together with its annexures' does not change the subject, so the singular proposal takes 'is'. The waiting began on Monday and continues, so it needs the present perfect continuous 'has been waiting', which marks duration from the past to now. 'Are' wrongly agrees with the annexures, and 'is waiting' misses the duration that 'since Monday' requires.
items.question: Fill in the blanks: The proposal, together with its annexures, ___ ready, and the team ___ waiting for approval since Monday.

items.explanation: Evasive means deliberately avoiding giving information, which both clauses require: the question was direct, and it had to be asked three times, showing intent to avoid. Vague, unclear and ambiguous describe the words themselves, not the deliberate avoidance, and a reply can be vague without the speaker trying to hide anything.
items.question: Fill in the blank: His reply was ___, giving nothing away although the question was direct, and the interviewer had to ask it three times before getting any answer at all.

items.explanation: Under the stated convention, 'data' is plural, so 'The data are clear on this point' is correct. The other sentences have errors: 'datas' is not a word; 'Each of the data' is singular and needs 'was'; 'The data is' uses a singular verb with plural 'data'.
options: The datas shows a clear trend.
Each of the data were checked.
The data is clear on this point.
The data are clear on this point.
items.question: In this item, 'data' is treated as a plural noun. Which sentence is grammatically correct?
items.stream_verdict: DEFECT: Ambiguity: the item hinges on 'data' as plural without stating the convention, so options A and B are both defensible.

items.explanation: Complement means to complete or add to something, which fits a report that completes the new policy, while compliment means to praise, which does not fit. Discrete means separate or individual, which fits a single word that on its own could change a clause's meaning, while discreet means careful or prudent in behaviour, which describes a person rather than a word's effect. Only option D gets both words right.
items.question: Fill in the blanks: The committee's report will ___ the new policy, and its wording must be precise, since a single ___ word could change the meaning of a clause.

items.explanation: Q follows S1 because it dates the line's opening. R follows Q because 'its stations' are the line's stations. S follows R because 'those stops' are the bus stops in R. P follows S because 'these passengers' are the line's passengers, placed as a contrast with the bus past. T comes last because it refers to 'the passengers who once relied on those buses', which needs P to have introduced those passengers, and it looks beyond the current line. QRSTP puts the second-line request before the passengers who make it have been introduced.
items.question: S1: The new metro line changed how the suburb commutes. S6: The line now carries more passengers than the old bus network did. Arrange P, Q, R, S, T in proper order. P. These passengers once relied on buses that took twice as long. Q. The line opened in March after two years of trials. R. Its stations were built around the old bus stops. S. Those stops had served the suburb for fifty years. T. The passengers who once relied on those buses now ask for a second line to serve the suburbs beyond the old stops.

items.explanation: The first differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, rising by 2 each time, so the next differences are 13 and 15. The next two terms are 35 + 13 = 48 and 48 + 15 = 63, and their sum is 48 + 63 = 111. 48 alone is only the first missing term, and stopping after one difference misses the second step entirely.
items.question: Find the next term in the series, and then the term after that: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?, ?. What is the sum of the two missing terms?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Number Series

items.explanation: The first differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, rising by 2 each time, so the next differences are 11 and 13. The next two terms are 29 + 11 = 40 and 40 + 13 = 53, and their sum is 40 + 53 = 93. 40 alone is only the first missing term, and 80 comes from doubling the first missing term instead of continuing the differences.
items.question: Find the next term in the series, and then the term after that: 5, 8, 13, 20, 29, ?, ?. What is the sum of the two missing terms?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Number Series

items.explanation: Alternate terms form two series: 3, 8, 13 increase by 5, and 7, 11 increase by 4. The next term continues the second series: 11 + 4 = 15.
items.question: Find the next term in the series: 3, 7, 8, 11, 13, ?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Number Series

items.explanation: The gaps grow by 1 going backwards: Z to X is 2, X to U is 3, U to Q is 4, Q to L is 5, so the next gaps are 6 and 7. L minus 6 is F, and F minus 7 is Y. F is only the sixth term, so stopping after one step lands on it, and the other options are one letter either side of the seventh term.
items.question: Find the next letter in the series, and then the letter after that: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?, ?. What is the second of the two missing letters, the seventh term of the series?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Letter Series

items.explanation: Shift MOUSE by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 to get NQXWJ, then reverse it to get JWXQN. NQXWJ is the trap for solvers who forget the reversal, ESUOM is the trap for solvers who only reverse the word, and FUXSR comes from applying the shifts in reverse order. The worked example confirms the rule: shifting LION gives MKRR, reversed to RRKM.
items.question: In a code, letters are shifted forward by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 places in order and the result is then reversed. LION is written as RRKM. How is MOUSE written?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.explanation: The first letters descend by 2 (Q, O, M, K, I), the digits rise by 1, and the third letter sits 3, 7, 11, 15, 19 places after the first letter, so the gap itself grows by 4. The missing term is therefore MN#3X4~4. MN#3W4~4 and MN#3Y4~4 get the easy progressions right and guess the accelerating rule, and KN#3X4~4 slips one step on the first letter.
items.question: Find the missing term in the sequence: QR#1T2~2, OP#2V3~3, ______, KL#4Z5~5, IJ#5\6~6.
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.explanation: Y is the brother of Z, and Z is the mother of W, so Y is W's uncle. U is Y's child, so U and W are children of a brother and a sister, which makes them cousins. 'Sister' would require U and W to share a parent, which they do not, and 'niece' would require U to be the child of W's sibling.
items.question: X is the daughter of Y. Y is the brother of Z. Z is the mother of W. Y is also the father of U. How is U related to W?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.explanation: Y is the sister of Z, so X, Y's son, is Z's nephew. W is Z's daughter, so X and W are cousins. 'Nephew' describes X's relation to Z, not to W, and 'brother' would need X and W to share a parent.
items.question: X is the son of Y. Y is the sister of Z. Z has only one child, W, the daughter of Z's spouse V. How is X related to W?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.explanation: 36, 54, 72 and 90 are all multiples of 18 with digit sum 9: 36, 54, 72 and 90 are 18 x 2, 18 x 3, 18 x 4 and 18 x 5. 48 is a multiple of 3 but not of 18, and its digit sum is 12, so it is the only one failing both conditions at once. Checking divisibility by 3 alone leaves 48 looking ordinary, which is why both conditions must be checked.
items.question: Find the odd one out: 36, 54, 72, 48, 90.
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Odd One Out

items.explanation: A teacher's defining action is to teach, so a judge's defining action is to decide cases, and Judge : Decide bears the same person-to-action relation. Court is where a judge works, law is what a judge applies, and robe is what a judge wears, so each distractor instantiates a different relation: place, subject and clothing.
items.question: Teacher : Teach bears the relation of a person to their defining action. Which of the following pairs bears the same relation?

items.explanation: Some managers are leaders, all leaders are decision-makers, and no decision-maker is impulsive, so those managers are not impulsive. Conclusion II is too strong: only some managers are leaders.
items.question: Statements: Some managers are leaders. All leaders are decision-makers. No decision-maker is impulsive. Conclusions: I. Some managers are not impulsive. II. All managers are decision-makers.

items.explanation: Both moves need buyers to respond to the price signal: the cut must change choices, and the advertising must reach buyers who will act on the lower price. If buyers were not sensitive enough for a 10% cut to change their choice, neither the cut nor the advertising of it would win buyers. That buyers value the product, that rivals will not cut further, and that costs will fall as sales rise do not by themselves make buyers respond.
options: Buyers value this product more than rivals' products
Competitors will not cut their prices further
Buyers are sensitive enough to price for a 10% cut to change their choice
The firm's costs will fall as sales rise
items.question: A firm will cut prices by 10% to attract more buyers, and will also double its advertising. Which of the following must be assumed for both decisions to make sense?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Statement and Assumption

items.explanation: The correct option names an alternative cause and shows that the improvement tracks that cause rather than the hiring. Each of the first two options gives only one of those two facts, and the third does not challenge the conclusion.
options: The factory also installed faster machines in the same month, and output rose most on the lines where the new machines were installed.
The factory also installed faster machines in the same month.
Output rose most on the lines where the new machines were installed.
Output is important for the factory's profits.
items.question: After the factory hired more workers, its output rose and the number of defects fell. The manager concludes that hiring more workers caused both improvements. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the manager's conclusion?
items.stream_verdict: REBUILD: Single obvious principle: a common cause explains all three rises. One obvious principle, weak distractors.
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Cause and Effect

items.explanation: The net movement north is 9 - 3 = 6 km and the net movement east is 12 - 4 = 8 km. The distance from the start is the square root of 36 + 64, which is 10 km, in the north-east direction.
items.question: A person walks 9 km north, then 12 km east, then 3 km south, then 4 km west. How far is the person from the starting point, and in which direction?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Direction Sense

items.explanation: The three turns sum to one quarter-turn anticlockwise: left, left and right cancel to a single left. Working backwards, the starting direction is one quarter-turn clockwise from the ending direction, so starting from East the person began facing South. The second person starts facing the opposite direction, North, and makes the same turns, so she turns one quarter-turn anticlockwise from North and ends facing West. The unknown start cannot be found by simulating forwards, since the start is what is missing: it has to be worked out backwards from the ending.
items.question: A person makes three turns: left, left, right, in that order, and ends facing East. She started facing an unknown direction. Which direction did she start facing? A second person starts facing the opposite direction and makes the same three turns. Which direction does the second person face? Give the two directions in order, first person then second person.
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Direction Sense

items.explanation: No absolute position is given, so call A's starting position a. Then B starts at a + 18, C sits at a + 4 and D sits at a + 14, so there are (a + 14) - (a + 4) - 1 = 9 people between C and D, and the unknown a cancels out. The moves confirm the picture rather than changing it: A moves to a + 3, immediately to the left of C, and B moves to a + 15, immediately to the right of D. Counting from the moved A or B instead of from C and D gives 10 or 11, and 7 comes from subtracting the two moves from the original 17 between A and B and then miscounting the C and D offsets.
items.question: In a row of 60 people, A sits to the left of B with 17 people between them. C sits 4 places to the right of A, and D sits 4 places to the left of B. A moves 3 places to the right and B moves 3 places to the left. C and D stay where they are. How many people sit between C and D now?

items.explanation: The clocks drift apart by 5 minutes every hour, 3 lost by one and 2 gained by the other, so a full hour of difference takes 60 divided by 5, or 12 hours. By then the slow clock has lost 12 times 3, or 36 minutes, so it shows 8 PM less 36 minutes, which is 7:24 PM. The 8:24 PM reading is the fast clock's, not the slow one's, and 10 hours gives only 50 minutes of drift.
items.question: A slow clock loses 3 minutes every hour and a fast clock gains 2 minutes every hour. Both are set right at 8 AM. After how many hours do the two clocks first differ by exactly one hour, and what does the slow clock then show? Give the hours and the slow clock's reading in order.

items.explanation: The 100th day is 99 days after 1 January, and 99 leaves a remainder of 1 on division by 7, since 99 is 14 x 7 + 1, so the day is one day after Monday, Tuesday. The 200th day is 199 days after 1 January, and 199 leaves a remainder of 3 on division by 7, since 199 is 28 x 7 + 3, so the day is three days after Monday, Thursday. Tuesday alone answers only the first half, and Friday comes from miscounting the remainder for the 200th day.
items.question: 1 January 2024 was a Monday. What day of the week was the 100th day of 2024, and what day of the week was the 200th day of 2024? Give the two days in order.

items.explanation: The arrangement is B, G, D, E, F, A, C in seats 1 to 7. Between B in seat 1 and A in seat 6 there are 4 people: G, D, E and F. The middle of seven seats is seat 4, which is E, and the person immediately to the left of E is D.
items.passage: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, sit in a row facing north. B sits at the left end. G sits immediately to the right of B. D sits immediately to the right of G. E sits immediately to the right of D. A sits second to the right of E. F sits immediately to the left of A. C sits at the right end.
items.question: How many people sit between B and A, and who sits immediately to the left of the person in the middle of the row? Give the count first, then the person.
items.stream_verdict: REBUILD: Single-step lookup: the seating is fully specified in the passage, so the solver only reads off the middle seat. No deduction.
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Seating Arrangement

items.explanation: The full row is B, G, D, E, F, A, C from left to right, which is determined only by combining all the clues: no single clue fixes more than one seat. A is in position 6, so two places to the left is position 4, which is E. The other options sit next to A or at the wrong distance, and they are the traps for solvers who count one place instead of two.
items.question: Who sits second to the left of A?
items.topic: Analytical and Logical Reasoning - Seating Arrangement

items.explanation: Apply the changes in order: 600 x 0.80 = 480, then 480 x 1.25 = 600, then 600 x 0.90 = 540. The net factor is 0.80 x 1.25 x 0.90 = 0.90, so the final price is Rs 540. 600 is the price after two changes, 480 applies only the first fall, and 630 comes from adding the percentages instead of compounding them.
items.question: A price of Rs 600 falls by 20%, then rises by 25%, and then falls by 10% again. What is the final price?

items.explanation: Revenue is 1260 x 30 = Rs 37,800 against a cost of 1500 x 20 = Rs 30,000, so profit is Rs 7,800, or 26%. If none had been spoilt, revenue would be 1500 x 30 = Rs 45,000, profit Rs 15,000, or 50%. 32% in the first place comes from counting only 120 spoilt articles, and 20% comes from selling the rest at Rs 26 instead of Rs 30.
items.question: A trader buys 1,500 articles at Rs 20 each. 240 articles are spoilt. The rest are sold at Rs 30 each. What is the profit percentage, and what would it have been if none of the articles had been spoilt? Give the two percentages in order.

items.explanation: The time is 4500 x 100 / (15000 x 10) = 3 years. The simple interest on Rs 15,000 at 12 percent for 3 years is 15000 x 12 x 3 / 100 = Rs 5,400.
items.question: A sum of Rs 15,000 at 10 percent simple interest earns Rs 4,500. How many years did it take, and what simple interest would the same sum earn at 12 percent per annum for the same period? Give the number of years first, then the interest.
items.stream_verdict: REBUILD: Mechanical single-interest chain: one formula applied to two rates and a flat comparison. One concept, no non-obvious step.

items.explanation: CI minus SI for 2 years is P x R^2 / 100^2, so 200 = P x 100 / 10,000, giving P = Rs 20,000. The simple interest is 20,000 x 10 x 2 / 100 = Rs 4,000, so the compound interest is 4,000 + 200 = Rs 4,200. Rs 10,000 comes from dividing by 2 instead of squaring the rate, and Rs 40,000 from using 5% instead of 10%.
items.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs 200. What is the sum, and what is the compound interest on it for 2 years? Give the two amounts in order.

items.explanation: The total is 12 x 35 = 420. Removing 20 and 40 leaves 360 spread over 10 numbers, so the remaining average is 360 / 10 = 36. The two removed numbers average (20 + 40) / 2 = 30. 37 comes from removing only one of the two numbers, and 35 is the original average, which the removal changes.
items.question: The average of 12 numbers is 35. Two numbers, 20 and 40, are removed. What is the average of the remaining numbers, and what is the average of the two removed numbers? Give the two averages in order.

items.explanation: The shifted values sum to 720 minus 100, or 620, and the ratios 2 : 5 and 3 : 2 combine to 6 : 15 : 10, or 31 parts, so each part is 20. Let y - 10 = 300. Then x - 40 = 120 and z - 50 = 200, so x = 160, y = 310 and z = 250, and x + y = 470. The ratios apply to the shifted values, not the originals: applying them to the originals gives 487.74. Solving for x alone gives 160, which answers the wrong question.
items.question: Three numbers x, y and z sum to 720. If x is reduced by 40, y by 10 and z by 50, then (x - 40) : (y - 10) = 2 : 5 and (y - 10) : (z - 50) = 3 : 2. Find x + y.

items.explanation: The first leg takes 150 / 50 = 3 hours and the second takes 150 / 75 = 2 hours, so the whole journey takes 5 hours. Total distance is 300 km, so average speed is 300 / 5 = 60 km/h. 62.5 km/h is the simple average of 50 and 75, the trap for solvers who average the speeds instead of dividing total distance by total time.
items.question: A car travels 150 km at 50 km/h and then 150 km at 75 km/h. How long does the whole journey take, and what is its average speed for the whole journey? Give the time and the speed in order.

items.explanation: Convert each pair to hourly rates: A + B do 960 / (6 x 8) = 20 units an hour, B + C do 12, and A + C do 16. Solving gives A's rate as 12 units an hour, so A alone needs 960 / (12 x 8) = 10 days at 8 hours a day. Treating days as the unit without rescaling the hours gives 6 days, and forgetting the final hours conversion gives 8 days.
items.question: A and B work 8 hours a day and complete a job in 6 days. B and C work 5 hours a day and complete the same job in 16 days. A and C work 6 hours a day and complete the same job in 10 days. How many days will A take to complete the job alone, working 8 hours a day?

items.explanation: Copper is 30 x 0.60 + 20 x 0.90 = 36 kg in 50 kg of mixture, so the first mixture is 72% copper. Removing 10 kg removes 10 x 0.72 = 7.2 kg of copper, leaving 28.8 kg. Adding 10 kg of pure copper gives 38.8 kg of copper in 50 kg, so the final percentage is 38.8 / 50 = 77.6%. 72% is the percentage before the replacement, and 75% is the simple average of 60% and 90%.
items.question: 30 kg of an alloy with 60% copper is mixed with 20 kg of an alloy with 90% copper. Then 10 kg of the mixture is removed and replaced with 10 kg of pure copper. What is the percentage of copper in the final mixture?

items.explanation: P(one white and one black) is (4 x 6 x 2) / (10 x 9) = 48/90 = 8/15. P(at least one white) is 1 - P(both black) = 1 - (6/10 x 5/9) = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3. The conditional probability is (8/15) / (2/3) = 4/5. 8/15 is the unconditional probability, the trap for solvers who ignore the given information, and 2/3 is the probability of the condition itself.
items.question: A bag has 4 white balls and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Given that at least one of the balls drawn is white, what is the probability that one ball is white and the other is black?

items.explanation: Weight each group by its die probability and by its share of girls: the joint probabilities are 7/50, 2/25, 6/25, so the total probability of a girl is 23/50. By Bayes, the probability of group Y given a girl is 2/25 / 23/50 = 4/23. 7/23 and 12/23 are the Bayes figures for the other two groups, and 1/5 is the unweighted share of girls in group Y, the trap for solvers who skip the die weights.
items.question: A group is chosen by rolling a fair die: the roll gives group X with probability 1/5, group Y with probability 2/5 and group Z with probability 2/5. group X has 7 girls and 3 boys; group Y has 2 girls and 8 boys; group Z has 6 girls and 4 boys. A child is then picked at random from the chosen group and turns out to be a girl. What is the probability that she was picked from group Y?

items.explanation: The odd positions are 1, 3 and 5. Choose 2 of the 3 odd positions for the vowels I and E, in 3 times 2, or 6 ways, and arrange the remaining four letters S, S, T and R in the remaining four places, in 4! divided by 2!, or 12 ways, giving 6 times 12, or 72 arrangements. 144 comes from doubling the vowel placements instead of counting them once, and 36 comes from placing the vowels without permuting I and E.
items.question: In how many ways can the letters of SISTER be arranged so that the vowels occupy only the odd positions?

items.explanation: No single condition fixes the number: the divisibility, the digit sum and the range must all hold at once, and only 35 satisfies all three. Each distractor satisfies two of the conditions and fails the third, which is the trap for solvers who check only one condition.
items.question: A two-digit number is divisible by 5, its digit sum is 8, and it is odd. Find the number.

items.explanation: Combine the logs and solve the resulting quadratic, then test each root against the domain: every log argument must be positive. One root makes an argument zero or negative, so it is extraneous and must be rejected, leaving x = 3. -3 is the extraneous root, the trap for solvers who solve the quadratic and stop.
items.question: Solve for x: log2(x - 1) = 3 - log2(x + 1).

items.explanation: The 45-degree angle gives AB = CD + BC = 9 + 3 = 12 cm, because the horizontal offset equals the height. Area is then (12 + 9) / 2 x 3 = 31.5 sq cm. 36 sq cm treats the trapezium as a rectangle of sides AB and BC, and 21 cm for AB adds both bases instead of adding the height to the shorter base.
items.question: In a trapezium, AB is parallel to CD, angle ABC is 90 degrees and angle BAD is 45 degrees. CD is 9 cm and BC is 3 cm. Find the area of the trapezium and the length AB. Give the area and the length in order.

items.explanation: The lights meet every LCM(24, 36, 48) = 144 seconds. The first joint change after 6:15:00 AM is at 6:17:24 AM, the second at 6:19:48 AM, and the third at 6:22:12 AM. 6:17:24 AM is the trap for solvers who stop at the first joint change, and 6:19:48 AM stops at the second.
items.question: Three traffic lights change at intervals of 24, 36 and 48 seconds. If all three change together at 6:15:00 AM, at what time will they change together for the third time after that?

items.explanation: The slope alone does not fix the intercept, and the point alone does not fix the slope. Together they give y = 2x, which passes through the origin. Either statement alone is the trap for solvers who assume one condition fixes a line.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.question: Does the line pass through the origin? Statement I: the slope of the line is 2. Statement II: the line passes through the point (1, 2).

items.explanation: In Rajasthan 70% of the population is above the index, with a male to female ratio of 5:2, so males above the index are 70 x 5/7 = 50% of the total population. Since that is 1.2 lakh, the total population is 2.4 lakh. Below the index are 30% of the population, with a male to female ratio of 2:1, so females below the index are 30 x 1/3 = 10% of the total, which is 0.24 lakh.
items.question: The male population above the educational index in Rajasthan is 1.2 lakh. What is the female population below the educational index in Rajasthan, approximately?

items.explanation: Males below the index are 15% of the population times 3 of 4, or 11.25% of the whole population, and males above it are 85% times 7 of 10, or 59.5% of the whole population. Total males are therefore 70.75% of the population, and the above-index share of males is 59.5 divided by 70.75, or 84.1%. 15.9% is the below-index share, which answers the opposite question, and 85% is the share of the whole population above the index, not of males.
items.question: What is the male population above the educational index in Madhya Pradesh as a percentage of the total male population of Madhya Pradesh?

items.explanation: Profit margin is (revenue - cost) / revenue. The margins are 2019: 12.50%; 2020: 25.00%; 2021: 15.79%; 2022: 23.08%. The highest is 2020 at 25.00%. 2022 has the second-highest margin, and the year with the largest revenue is not the year with the highest margin, since margin depends on the gap between revenue and cost, not on revenue alone.
items.question: Delta Ltd's revenue and cost are shown in the chart. In which year was the profit margin (profit as a percentage of revenue) the highest, and what was that margin? Give the year and the margin in order.

items.explanation: Scoring fairly while leaving the early access in place lets one bidder keep an advantage the others never had, so the tender stays unfair even with honest scoring. Extending the deadline is the cost of undoing that advantage, and it is the only way every bidder gets the same documents for the same time. Only the third option refuses the favour, scores on the published criteria, notes the request, and reissues the documents to all bidders on an extended deadline. Favouring the firm because it is competent lets competence decide a matter the rules reserve for a scored process.
options: Favour the firm, since it is competent
Refuse, score every bid on the published criteria, and note the request
Refuse, score every bid on the published criteria, note the request, extend the deadline, and reissue the documents to all bidders
Score fairly but say nothing about the request or the early documents
items.question: A colleague asks you to favour their friend's firm in a tender, saying the firm is competent. The tender rules require scoring on published criteria. The friend's firm has already been given the tender documents early by mistake. The tender closes tomorrow, and reissuing the documents means extending the deadline. What should you do?

items.explanation: The manager has already signed, so refusing to countersign without telling finance leaves the payment to go through on the manager's signature alone. Only the second option stops it: you refuse, record the reason, and escalate to finance so the payment is stopped. Refusing without a record leaves the request undocumented, and signing because the amount is small approves a false record for the sake of convenience.
options: Sign it, since the amount is small and the work will come later
Refuse to sign, record the reason, and escalate to finance so the payment is stopped
Refuse to sign but keep no record of the request
Sign it and tell the vendor to hurry up with the work
items.question: Your manager asks you to approve a vendor invoice for work that was not done, saying the vendor will do the work later. The vendor is a friend of your manager, and the amount is small. The manager has already signed the invoice, so your refusal alone does not stop payment. What should you do?

items.explanation: The team's refusal to sign a core-hours agreement cannot veto an accommodation the policy allows, and judging on attendance penalises the disability itself. Only the fourth option judges the member on output, accommodates the hours, and sets the core window by management decision, which gives the team a fixed time for meetings without asking the team to vote on someone else's accommodation. Judging on output while refusing the hours fails the accommodation, and refusing the hours because the team complains lets the team's convenience decide it.
options: Judge them on attendance, since they are rarely in the office
Judge them on output but refuse the flexible hours
Refuse the hours, since the team complains about rescheduling
Judge them on output, accommodate the hours as policy allows, and set the core window by management decision so the team is not disrupted
items.question: A team member with a disability asks for flexible hours. Their output is good, but they are rarely in the office at the same time as the team, and the team complains that meetings keep being rescheduled. Policy allows flexible hours only with a core-hours agreement, and the team refuses to sign one. How should you appraise them?

items.explanation: As manager you can act on what you observe yourself, so documenting the behaviour, speaking to the performer, inviting complaints and setting expectations is the right immediate response, and it does not depend on a formal complaint already existing. But the policy as written would block the next case, so it also needs amending so that documented manager observations can trigger a review. Option B does both halves. Option A does nothing. Option C punishes without process. Option D tells the victims to cope and tightens the very rule that caused the problem.
options: (Now: wait for a formal complaint. Change: none.)

(Now: document what you observed, speak to the performer, invite formal complaints and set expectations. Change: amend the policy so that documented manager observations can trigger a review even without a formal complaint.)
(Now: transfer the performer at once. Change: none.)
(Now: warn the team to avoid the performer. Change: require a formal complaint before any review.)
items.question: A top performer bullies colleagues in meetings. HR has no formal complaint on record, and the performer denies everything. HR policy says no action follows without a formal complaint, but you as manager can document behaviour you observe yourself. Which of the following best combines what you should do now with the change the policy needs?

items.explanation: Recalling the shipped packs costs more than the switch, so a recall is not the answer, but leaving the green label on them lets customers keep buying on a false assumption for two quarters. Only the second option stops the misleading sale without a recall: the switch runs over two quarters, the current packs are labelled honestly, the green label stops on new packs, and retailers are told to remove it. Switching without labelling the current packs leaves customers misled, labelling honestly but never switching keeps the misleading packs on sale indefinitely, and keeping the label because sales are rising lets sales decide a matter of honest labelling.
options: Keep the green label, since sales are rising
Switch to recyclable packaging over two quarters, label the current packs honestly, stop using the green label on new packs, and tell retailers to remove it
Switch to recyclable packaging but keep the current packs as they are
Label the packs honestly but never switch
items.question: Your product's packaging is not recyclable, although customers assume it is, and sales are rising on that assumption. Switching will take two quarters. The green label is already on packs shipped to retailers, and recalling them costs more than the switch itself. What should you do?

items.explanation: The affected buyers cannot be identified one by one, since they are small shops, so compensation has to travel through the retailers, and a private fix leaves them uncompensated. Only the third option fixes the machine, corrects the weights, pays the compensation through the retailers, and publishes how to claim, so the shops that were short-changed can actually get it back. Correcting the weights while saying nothing leaves them uncompensated, keeping the short packs on sale keeps selling underweight packs, and doing nothing because most buyers have not noticed lets their ignorance decide a matter of honest weights.
options: Do nothing, since most buyers have not noticed
Correct the weights but say nothing to buyers
Fix the machine, correct the weights, compensate the affected buyers through the retailers, and publish how to claim
Fix the machine but keep the short packs on sale
items.question: Your packs weigh 5% less than the label says. The error is in the filling machine, and only recent batches are affected. Most buyers have not noticed. The affected buyers are mostly small shops that cannot be identified individually. What should you do?

items.explanation: Stopping at once breaks supply for a problem a timeline could fix, and buying through an intermediary hides the origin instead of fixing it. The verified source costs more and is a single supplier, so switching to it alone trades one risk for another. Only the fourth option traces the chain, switches over a timeline, discloses the change, and dual-sources where possible, so the conflict risk is removed without putting the whole order on one supplier.
options: Continue buying, since you cannot prove a link
Stop buying at once with no alternative source
Buy through an intermediary so the origin is hidden
Trace the supply chain, switch to the verified source over a timeline, disclose the change, and dual-source where possible so no single supplier carries the whole order
items.question: Your raw material comes from a region affected by conflict, and you cannot be sure the purchase does not fund armed groups. The only verified source costs 30% more, and it is a single supplier, so switching to it alone creates a concentration risk. What should you do?

items.explanation: The client decides on renewal next week, so waiting two weeks for the colleague to return leaves the client deciding on a wrong report. Covering it up fixes the numbers while the client stays misled, and telling the manager without telling the colleague takes the choice out of the colleague's hands. Only the first option corrects the report now, tells the colleague on return, and helps them own the mistake, so the client gets the truth in time and the colleague still faces the consequence honestly.
options: Correct the client report now yourself, tell the colleague on their return, and help them own the mistake
Cover it up and fix it quietly
Tell the manager without telling the colleague first
Fix the report but hide the mistake from the client
items.question: A colleague made a mistake that will cost them a promotion if it is discovered. You could cover it up and fix it quietly. The mistake affects a client report that has already gone out. The colleague is on leave for two weeks, and the client is deciding on renewal next week. What should you do?
items.topic: Ethics - Personal Morality and Civic Responsibility

items.explanation: The client is deciding on renewal, so hiding the error misleads them, and blaming the process instead of stating the facts evades the question they asked. Naming the colleague by name embarrasses them again and tells the client nothing about the fix. Only the third option gives the client what they need to decide: the facts, how the error was fixed, and what will prevent a repeat, without naming a colleague who asked not to be named.
options: Hide the error, since the contract is at stake
State the facts and blame the colleague by name
State the facts without naming the colleague, focus on how it was fixed, and say what will prevent a repeat
Blame the process instead of stating the facts
items.question: A client asks about a colleague's error that embarrassed the colleague. You know the facts. The client is deciding whether to renew the contract. The colleague has asked you not to name them, and the client asks who made the error. What should you say?
items.topic: Ethics - Personal Morality and Civic Responsibility

items.explanation: Including a friend who does not meet the criteria so they get severance is fraud on the process, however kindly meant, and protecting your friends while laying off ten others instead is favouritism that breaks the criteria. Delaying and hiding the plan leaves people unable to plan their lives, and resigning in protest abandons the team to a manager who may be less fair without changing the outcome for the ten. Only the second option applies the criteria to everyone, explains the reasons, arranges severance and support, tells the safe friend why they are safe, and refuses the request to be included.
options: Resign in protest against the layoffs
Apply the criteria fairly to everyone, explain the reasons, arrange severance and support, tell the friend who does not meet the criteria why they are safe, and refuse the request to include them
Delay the layoffs and hide the plan from the team
Protect your friends and lay off ten others instead
items.question: You must lay off ten people in your team. The criteria are clear, but three of the ten are your friends. The criteria were set last month, and two of your friends meet them while one does not. The friend who does not meet the criteria has asked you to include them anyway so they get the severance. What should you do?
items.topic: Ethics - Personal Morality and Civic Responsibility
